The first bit of actually interacting with reference types in the CM+GC work. This forces us to build out a bunch of infrastructure, so I'm trying to keep this as minimal as possible by only supporting tuples of scalars. Follow up commits will introduce tuples of tuples and other reference-typed things like records and strings and arrays and all that.

:memo: alexcrichton submitted PR review:

Overall I personally still feel lost on this. I feel like much of what's here is likely to be necessary in one shape or another, such as the fact/trampoline.rs handling of primitives and general infrastructure for structs/etc, but the ABI calculations and "what types are used" infrastructure seems possibly to pretty radically change. For example I feel that there's still two major open questions:

  • How exactly to represent variants? If we go the "everything has a canonical type" route than all the rec-group matching/copying here is dead code and irrelevant.
  • Whether or not to "flatten" more. If we go the route of everything having a canonical type then it seems a bit silly to turn option<u8> into a (ref $option_u8) when passed as a parameter when in the linear memory ABI it's two scalars being passed which should be far more efficient.

These are pretty fundamental pieces of the ABI which I feel are currently unresolved, and I feel that they pretty heavily influence the implementation and what we land here. I'm not opposed necessarily to landing this and moving on that later, but this is 2kloc of new code which is pretty intense IMO and it's only the tip of the iceberg. I find it really hard to retroactively reason about vast amounts of new code when the underlying primitives change, and we've been burned quite a few times by refactoring the design of component-model-async at the spec level and the PR to implement in Wasmtime leaves a lot of vestiges of things that bite us later.

So question for you: what would you like the plan to be on this? Land this now as-is and possibly refactor later? If so what would be the main purpose of landing this in-tree?

:speech_balloon: alexcrichton created PR review comment:

fitzgen commented on PR #15051:

So question for you: what would you like the plan to be on this? Land this now as-is and possibly refactor later? If so what would be the main purpose of landing this in-tree?

My goal is to fill out the lifting/lowering from GC objects paths, which I think are the most critical things to shake out and are actually going to look pretty similar regardless anything I can imagine changing about the CM+GC proposal.

It is true that the rec group cloning would largely go away with an "everything has a single canonical type" potential future, but (a) I think that is actually the simplest and most self-contained code here, and (b) it would be replaced by "generate the canonical core types for this CM type" code that actually would be somewhat similar, and similarly self-contained.

I would say there are two primary motivations for landing it in tree, rather than e.g. a bytecodealliance/wasmtime-cm-gc fork:

  1. To make it easier for toolchains to start playing with it and giving us implementation and spec feedback.
  2. To do incremental reviews and build a shared understanding/theory of the code, rather than for me to go off on my own for a while and then come back with a giant code dump. (This approach has never worked well for the project IMO).

fitzgen commented on PR #15051:

And regarding variants needing to change or whether to flatten more, I don't think that really changes much about the GC source/destination changes, which, as I said, are the most fundamental changes to shake out here. Variants aren't even implemented in this PR and are still the same todo! they already were, and the flattening feels like a bridge we can cross if/when we get to it.
